prompt: Turn this rough painted sketch into a photorealistic industrial-design studio render of one compact handheld camera. Keep the exact same 3/4 front view, composition and proportions: rounded hand grip on the left, lens on the front right, dark viewfinder block top rear, dark cylindrical dial block top right. Concept: entropy, light meeting a black hole. Core body: deep matte black, velvety, light-absorbing paint. Over it run two plump inflated light-grey tubes with round cross-sections in satin soft-touch paint. They form the rounded grip on the left, rise over the top, twist and cross each other in a loose braid between the viewfinder and dial blocks, then curve down onto the front and wrap the lens as one thick continuous light-grey torus ring. On the ring's inner edge the grey fades to black and the surface sinks inward into the black body, as if the light is swallowed by the lens. Lens: a real camera lens about 35 mm in diameter in the centre of the ring, black anodized knurled barrel, dark coated front glass with concentric inner reflections and a faint purple-green sheen. Solid painted material only, no LED, no glow. Clearly visible: round black shutter button on top of the grip; small USB-C port in a black inset on the outer left side of the grip; knurled black cap on the dial. Clean surfaces, generous fillets, crisp part lines, reads as a 3D-printed, painted design model. One single camera fully in frame, centred, seamless pure white background, soft key light from upper left, soft contact shadow, sharp focus. No text, no logos, no hands, no extra objects.
